rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Hearing On Verified Petition For Declaratory Judgment; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for September 8, 2026, line 1. PETITIONER JASON SCUTT'S Petition For Declaratory Judgment. Petitioner Jason Russell Scutt's petition for declaratory judgment is denied. Scutt seeks a judgment declaring that certain articles of organization for Octopus Suite Suite LLC are lawful, that its proposed operating structure is lawful, and that operation of the proposed company would not constitute the unauthorized practice of any licensed profession. "The fundamental basis of declaratory relief is the existence of an actual, present controversy over a proper subject." (In re Tobacco Cases II (2015) 240 Cal.App.4th 779, 804 (internal quotations omitted.) "Whether a claim presents an 'actual controversy' within the meaning of Code of Civil Procedure section 1060 is a question of law..." (Envt'l Defense Project of Sierra County v. County of Sierra (2008) 158 Cal.App.4th 877, 885.) "[A] 'complaint for declaratory relief is legally sufficient if it sets forth facts showing the existence of an actual controversy relating to the legal rights and duties of the parties.' " (In re Tobacco Cases II, 240 Cal.App.4th at p. 804.) Scutt does not present any actual, present controversy. There are insufficient facts from which the court could render any reasoned decision. By not naming any defendants, Scutt's judgment would not bind any party but Scutt. The court therefore concludes that Scutt has not presented a proper basis for a judicial declaration. Scutt essentially asks for an advisory opinion that the court may not give. (See Nisei Farmers League v. Labor & Workforce Development Agency (2019) 30 Cal.App.5th 997, 1022-1023.) Scutt is directed to prepare a proposed judgment denying the petition. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Further Responses To Form Interrogatories, Set One, From Defendant Asjk, Llc Dba The Avenues Transitional Care Center
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for September 8, 2026, line 9. PLAINTIFFS' Motion To Compel Further Responses To Form Interrogatories, Set One, From Defendant Asjk, LLC. Plaintiffs Phuoc Trinh et al.'s ("Trinh") motion to compel defendant ASJK LLC to make further responses to form interrogatories, set one, numbers 12.1 and 12.6, is granted and sanctions are awarded. Form interrogatory 12.1 asks for identifying information for each individual who witnessed the incident, made statements at the scene of the incident, etc. It has four discrete subparts. The incident here is a fall. ASJK responded by referring Trinh to the entire medical record, invoking Code of Civil Procedure, Sec. 2030.230. But an invocation of that section is ambiguous in this context and where the interrogatory has subparts; which witnesses does ASJK contend saw the fall? Which made a statement at the scene of the incident? Does ASJK contend that every person who treated Trinh is a witness to the incident? The response is not complete and straightforward, and moreover ASJK has not specified which records within the medical records contain responsive information. (See Fuss v. Superior Court for Los Angeles County (1969) 273 Cal.App.2d 807, 817.) ASJK shall amend. Form interrogatory 12.6 asks if any report was made regarding the incident. ASJK's invocation of the entire medical record in response suffers from the same deficiencies just identified. ASJK shall amend. Verified amendments shall be made within 10 days of notice of entry of this order. ASJK's discovery position lacks substantial justification and it shall pay $1300 in reasonable sanctions to Trinh within 30 days of notice of entry of this order. rulings.Case Title: AMERICAN EXPRESS NATIONAL BANK VS. ANGELO CARAS A/K/A CREATOR MAREKETER ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion Of Defendant Angelo J. Cartas To Compel Arbitration And Stay Proceedings; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for September 8, 2026, line 12. DEFENDANT ANGELO CARTAS' Motion To Compel Arbitration And Stay Proceedings. Defendant's motion to compel arbitration and stay this case is GRANTED. "The petitioner bears the burden of proving the existence of a valid arbitration agreement by the preponderance of the evidence, and a party opposing the petition bears the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence any fact necessary to its defense." (Engalla v. Permanente Medical Group, Inc. (1997) 15 Cal.4th 951, 972.) In this case, defendant establishes that the parties entered into an enforceable arbitration agreement. Plaintiff's standard cardmember agreement provides that either party "may elect to resolve any claim by individual arbitration." (Cartas Decl., Ex. A.) Per the agreement, the parties shall arbitrate in front of the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") because defendant (the electing party) chooses that forum. Plaintiff's argument that defendant must file a claim with AAA to commence the arbitration process does not make sense. Plaintiff brought the "claim" against defendant and defendant is not currently seeking affirmative relief. In other words, defendant has no "claim" to file. Plaintiff is in the best position to commence the arbitration process and describe the dispute and monetary relief sought. There is no basis for this court to set a status conference. AAA shall resolve the arbitration fee issues. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA)
